messages.subject: ShinyStan v2.0.0 now available
messages.body_plain:
We're happy to announce that a new version of ShinyStan is now officially available. For those of you not familiar with ShinyStan <http://mc-stan.org/interfaces/shinystan.html>, it is a graphical user interface for exploring Stan models (and more generally any MCMC output).

ShinyStan v2.0.0 has a new look and a lot of new features. It also has a new(ish) name. You can now find the ShinyStan GUI in the shinystan R package (both had formerly been shinyStan).

1) Installation

- From CRAN:

install.packages("shinystan")

- If you want a version with a few minor typos fixed you can install from Github:

devtools::install_github("stan-dev/shinystan", build_vignettes = TRUE)

(Note: for those of you who have the old version installed, because of the name change the new version will not overwrite the old one. So once you have the new version installed and check that it's working we recommend removing the old version by running remove.packages("shinyStan").)

2) News

This update contains a lot of changes, both in terms of new features added, greater UI stability, and an entirely new look. Some release notes can be found on GitHub (release notes <https://github.com/stan-dev/shinystan/releases/tag/v2.0.0>) and there are also some instructions for getting started on the ShinyStan wiki page <https://github.com/stan-dev/shinystan/wiki>. So you can check those out, but I'll give two of my favorite additions here:

> - The new suite of interactive HMC/NUTS diagnostic plots.
>
>  -The deploy_shinystan function, which lets you easily deploy ShinyStan apps for your models to RStudio's ShinyApps  <https://www.shinyapps.io/>hosting service. Each of your apps (i.e. each of your models) will have a unique URL. To use this feature please also install the shinyapps package: devtools::install_github("rstudio/shinyapps").

3) Questions, comments, feature requests, bug reports

Please let us know! The plan is to release a minor update with bug fixes and other minor tweaks in a month or so. So if you find anything we should fix or change please post to the issue tracker <https://github.com/stan-dev/shinystan/issues> on GitHub. You can also use the issue tracker for larger feature requests. For questions or to share any comments you can post here on the stan-users message board.

Thanks!

- Stan Development Team

P.S. One last thing before you go play with the new version. In the old version, calling launch_shinystan(stanfit)would not only launch the app but it would also save a shinystan object (sso) in your global environment. In the new version launch_shinystan is more similar to typical R functions in that it will only save the sso if you assign it to name. For example

name_for_sso <- launch_shinystan(stanfit)

will launch ShinyStan and, after exiting, you will have an sso with the name name_for_sso, whereas just using launch_shinystan(stanfit) won't keep the sso after quitting.
